description.value: A slung gut-skin bladder with a bound neck and a carrying harness of four cords, holding one half of a household ferment culture at the moment of a division. It was made new for the 2295 split of the sixth rib household, filled by pouring, fed alongside its other half for nine nights and then carried away, all of which is the standard sequence. The skin is intact, the neck binding has been renewed once, and the culture in it is alive and is not part of the accession. It is catalogued as a ceremonial vessel because a bladder made for a division is never afterwards used for storage, and this rule is absolute.
